questions.question:
Assertion (A): The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme has become the largest microfinance project in the world.
Reason (R): NABARD introduced it in 1992 to promote rural credit through group savings and bank linkage.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution: Both statements are true. NABARD pioneered the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme in 1992, and it has indeed grown into the world's most extensive microfinance initiative.

questions.question: Which of the following government initiatives focuses on skill development to reduce open unemployment among youth in India?
questions.option_2: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
questions.solution: PMKVY, launched in 2015, is the flagship scheme for skill training of youth to make them more employable and reduce unemployment.

questions.question: ‘NISHTHA’ stands for _________.
questions.option_1: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment
questions.option_2: National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
questions.option_3: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
questions.option_4: National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment
questions.solution: NISHTHA stands for National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement. It is an integrated teacher training program to improve learning outcomes at the elementary level.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE about the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) of India?
i. One of the main objectives of the Zones Act was promotion of exports of goods and services.
ii. The Government of India announced the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) Policy in the year 2011.
iii. The SEZ Rules provided for different minimum land requirement for different classes of SEZs.
questions.solution: Statement ii is false. The SEZ Act was passed in 2005 and came into effect in 2006, not 2011.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Sukanya Samriddhi Account (SSA):
1. It was launched in 2015 under the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign.
2. The maximum deposit allowed in one financial year is ₹1.5 lakh.
3. It can be opened for a girl child until she attains 12 years of age.
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the SSA can only be opened for a girl child until the age of 10 years.

questions.question: How much percentage of the capital of MUDRA is contributed by SIDBI?
questions.solution: MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) was established as a wholly owned subsidiary (100% capital) of SIDBI.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (2005) provides work for how many days?
questions.solution: The MGNREGA, passed in 2005, guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. It aims to enhance livelihood security in rural areas.

questions.question: The ‘Urban Self Employment Programme’ and the ‘Urban Wage Employment Programme’ are the two special components of which poverty alleviation programme of India?
questions.solution: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in 1997 to provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed or underemployed poor. Its two main components were the Urban Self Employment Programme (USEP) and the Urban Wage Employment Programme (UWEP).

questions.question: Which of the following schemes adopts the One District One Product (ODOP) approach to reap the benefit of scale in terms of procurement of inputs, availing common services and marketing of products?
questions.option_2: Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
questions.option_3: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
questions.option_4: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI)
questions.solution: The PMFME scheme, launched under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, adopts the One District One Product (ODOP) approach. This helps micro-food processing units benefit from collective scaling in branding, marketing, and infrastructure.

questions.question: In which year did the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare of India launch the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) program?
questions.solution: The WIFS program was launched in 2012 to address the high prevalence of anaemia among adolescents (ages 10-19) in India by providing supervised weekly iron-folic acid tablets.

questions.question: How many cities are covered under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) scheme?
questions.solution: The AMRUT mission, launched in 2015, covers 500 cities across India. Its primary goal is to ensure that every household has access to a tap with an assured supply of water and a sewerage connection.

questions.question: When was the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) launched?
questions.solution: PMEGP was launched in 2008 by merging two earlier schemes (PMRY and REGP). It is a credit-linked subsidy scheme for setting up micro-enterprises and generating employment in both rural and urban areas.

questions.question: The government of India launched the New India Literacy Programme (NILP) for five years, covering which period?
questions.solution: The New India Literacy Programme (NILP) is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented from FY 2022-23 to 2026-27. It targets non-literates aged 15 years and above to provide foundational literacy and life skills.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes aims to provide an integrated property validation solution for rural India?
questions.solution: SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) uses drone technology to map residential land in villages, providing property cards to rural owners as a validation tool.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Twenty Point Programme (TPP):
1. It was launched in 1975.
2. The programme was revised in 1982, 1986, and 2006.
3. The main objective is to improve urban infrastructure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Twenty Point Programme primarily focuses on poverty alleviation and improving the quality of life for the rural poor and underprivileged.

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the objective of Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) Scheme, 2016?
questions.option_1: To provide financial assistance to entrepreneurs
questions.option_2: To provide free healthcare services to the unemployed
questions.option_3: To provide employment opportunities for rural women
questions.option_4: To encourage employers to create new jobs
questions.solution: The PMRPY scheme was designed to incentivise employers to create new employment by the Government paying the full employer's contribution towards EPF and EPS for new employees.

questions.question: Which of the following programmes of the Government of India aims to provide connectivity to unconnected habitations as part of a poverty reduction strategy?
questions.option_1: Prime Minister Rural Development Fellows Scheme
questions.solution: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), launched in 2000, aims to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected rural habitations to facilitate socio-economic development.

questions.question: What is the full form of MEDP?
questions.solution: MEDP stands for Micro Enterprise Development Programme. Supported by NABARD, it provides skill development training to Self Help Groups (SHGs) to help them start micro-enterprises.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana is for Indian citizens in the age group of ___________ .
questions.solution: The PMJJBY is a one-year life insurance scheme renewable from year to year, offering coverage for death due to any reason. It is available to people in the age group of 18 to 50 years.

questions.question: Rural Backyard Piggery Scheme was launched by which state government?
questions.solution: The Rural Backyard Piggery Scheme was launched by the Meghalaya government in 2022 to promote sustainable livelihoods through livestock farming and reduce the state's meat import deficit.

questions.question: Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) was launched in ___ .
questions.solution: The REGP was launched on April 1, 1995, by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) to generate employment opportunities in rural areas and small towns.

questions.question: Stand Up India scheme aims at supporting entrepreneurship to which community?
questions.solution: The Stand Up India scheme facilitates bank loans between 10 lakh and 1 crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up a greenfield enterprise.

questions.question: LPG subsidy to domestic consumers under PAHAL Scheme is given by which Ministry?
questions.option_1: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
questions.option_2: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.solution: The PAHAL (Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh) scheme, which transfers LPG subsidies directly into consumers' bank accounts, is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

questions.question: Under the Atal Pension Yojana, the pension returns are given after the subscriber turns ________ .
questions.solution: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) focuses on the unorganized sector. Subscribers receive a guaranteed minimum monthly pension ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after they reach the age of 60.

questions.question: The National Family Benefit Scheme was started in August ______ by the Government of India.
questions.solution: The National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) was introduced in August 1995 under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) to provide a lump sum grant to BPL households upon the death of the primary breadwinner.
